item.strong: SRS v1 · Software Requirements Specification (SRS) Overview for Bank Customer Onboarding

srs.title: Software Requirements Specification (SRS) Overview for Bank Customer Onboarding
srs.summary: This document outlines the software requirements specification for a bank customer onboarding application with KYC verification, secure document storage, and audit logs. The system must support 10,000 customers, include dual approval by onboarding and compliance staff, and integrate with the current
assumptions: The system will use V-CIP for remote customer identity verification as per E1.
The system will synchronize KYC records automatically with the existing customer management system.
Address verification will be done via a positive confirmation process as per E1 and E2.

findings.text: The process for verifying a customer's current address is described as an 'address verification letter', but the exact steps and validation criteria are not clearly defined in the answers.
The requirement to restrict transactions to the mobile number used for account opening is not fully detailed, particularly regarding how this will be enforced in the system.
The process of categorizing non-face-to-face customers as high-risk and the monitoring requirements are not clearly outlined in the answers.

risks.title: Security Risks
risks.text: The system must ensure secure document storage and audit logs, which could be vulnerable to breaches if not implemented properly.

risks.title: Compliance Risks
risks.text: The system must comply with the prescribed standards for V-CIP as per E1, which may require additional controls and documentation.

openIssues: How will the system handle changes to a customer's registered mobile number? The answers do not specify a process for this.
What are the specific steps for positive confirmation of the current address?
How will the system ensure that transactions are restricted to the mobile number used for account opening?

requirements.statement: The application must support remote verification of a customer's identity using V-CIP as the first option for non-face-to-face onboarding.
requirements.acceptance: V-CIP process is implemented and tested with real-time interaction validation, ensuring that interactions are not pre-recorded. The system must reject any account opening processif

requirements.statement: The application must automatically synchronize updates to a customer's KYC records across all relevant systems.
requirements.acceptance: A synchronization mechanism is implemented and tested, ensuring that changes in KYC records are reflected across the system within 1 minute of update.

requirements.statement: The application must verify a customer's current address through positive confirmation before allowing operations on the account.
requirements.acceptance: Positive confirmation methods such as address verification letters or contact point verification are implemented and tested, ensuring that address validation is completed before任何账

requirements.statement: The application must restrict transactions to the mobile number used for account opening, preventing use of alternate numbers for transaction OTP or updates.
requirements.acceptance: A restriction mechanism is implemented and tested, ensuring that only the mobile number used for account opening can be used for transaction-related activities.

requirements.statement: The application must support dual approval by onboarding and compliance staff for all customer onboarding processes.
requirements.acceptance: A dual approval workflow is implemented and tested, ensuring that both onboarding and compliance staff must approve the process before it is finalized.

requirements.statement: The application must store customer documents securely and ensure that access to these documents is restricted to authorized personnel only.
requirements.acceptance: A secure document storage system is implemented and tested, ensuring that all documents are encrypted and accessible only to authorized users.

requirements.statement: The application must maintain audit logs for all customer onboarding activities, including the date, time, and actions taken by each user.
requirements.acceptance: Audit logging is implemented and tested, ensuring that a detailed log of all onboarding-related activities is maintained and accessible for review.

requirements.statement: The application must ensure that the V-CIP process complies with RBI guidelines on cyber security and resilience framework for banks.
requirements.acceptance: V-CIP infrastructure is implemented and tested, ensuring compliance with RBI guidelines on cyber security and resilience, including secure network domains and data ownership.

requirements.statement: The application must monitor accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode for enhanced monitoring until identity verification is completed through V-CIP or face-to-face method.
requirements.acceptance: A monitoring system is implemented and tested, ensuring that accounts opened without V-CIP are subject to enhanced monitoring until identity verification is complete.

requirements.statement: The application must ensure that all transactions for non-face-to-face mode accounts are restricted to the mobile number used for account opening.
requirements.acceptance: A transaction restriction mechanism is implemented and tested, ensuring that only the mobile number used for account opening can be used for any transaction-related activities.

ranking.why: strict verification and validation: every build phase has a matching test phase
high regulation with evolving requirements: iterations plus V-Model verification gates
risk-driven loops for high uncertainty or technical risk
continuous secure deployment with automated security checks
short iterations absorb frequently changing requirements
rapid prototyping for small, low-risk systems

rejected.why: two processes to run; only pays off when requirements keep changing
testing comes late, so verification evidence arrives after design is locked
heavy risk analysis each loop is costly when requirements are clear
its value is continuous delivery, which this project needs little of
light documentation clashes with formal audit and sign-off
too little rigour for high-risk or regulated systems
